plain: Whitley Strieber, a writer known for his book Communion about his own encounters, says that in 1986 a scientist named Robert Sarbacher asked him to write out his whole experience. Strieber says he wrote it up at his cabin in upstate New York and shipped it to Sarbacher in Florida, and the next morning the delivery driver called to say "The recipient has expired": Sarbacher had died that night. Strieber tells the story twice in the same interview, and once he only stresses Sarbacher's request, without mentioning the death.
